outline.chapter_title: Governing Legal Framework: Louisiana's Strict Adherence Standard
outline.description: This chapter explicates the specific Louisiana statute (La. Rev. Stat. § 9:3550) governing the cancellation of financed insurance policies. It analyzes the statutory text regarding notice requirements and introduces the controlling judicial doctrine of 'strict adherence,' explaining why minor deviations can render a cancellation ineffective under state law.
subtopics: Statutory Text: Requirements for Notice and Certification under § 9:3550(G)(3)

Consequences of Defective Cancellation Procedures

outline.chapter_title: Issue I: The Requirement of Signature on Certification Notices
outline.description: This chapter focuses on the plaintiffs' first major argument: that the statute implicitly requires a human signature on the cancellation certification. It details GoAuto's automated procedure where emails precede physical signatures, analyzes the statutory silence on signatures, and explains the Fifth Circuit's reasoning in rejecting the necessity of a pre-cancellation signature.
subtopics: Plaintiffs' Argument: 'Certifying' Implies Individual Identification and Signature
Analysis of Statutory Silence and Lack of Explicit Signature Mandate
Review of Conflicting or Ambiguous Louisiana Case Law (Benitez vs. Others)
Corporate vs. Individual Certification: Interpreting 'The Company' as the Certifier
Judicial Restraint: Refusing to Add Requirements Not Found in the Statute

outline.chapter_title: Issue II: Constructive Receipt via Automated Web Services
outline.description: This chapter addresses the second critical issue: whether GoAuto legally 'received' the cancellation request when its computer system processed an email prior to any human handling or physical stamping. It contrasts traditional definitions of receipt with modern technological realities, validating electronic communication between corporate systems as sufficient for statutory compliance.
subtopics: The Statutory Trigger: Cancellation 'Upon Receipt' of Notice
Defining 'Receipt': Physical Possession vs. Electronic Delivery
The Mechanics of GoAuto's Web Service and Automated Cancellation Workflow
Rejection of the 'Private Carrier' Theory in Favor of Direct Electronic Receipt
Modernizing Statutory Interpretation for Corporate Computer Systems

outline.description: This final chapter covers the court's ultimate holding affirming the district court, its refusal to certify questions to the Louisiana Supreme Court, and the broader implications for insurance administration.
